packing: none: every struct is byte-packed, no alignment padding

semantics.dotnetTicks: i64 100ns ticks since 0001-01-01T00:00:00 (no time zone); mask off the top 2 bits (DateTimeKind) before use; 0 = empty

strings.fixed: one byte per character, NUL-padded to the declared length; the value ends at the first NUL (no NUL when the value fills the field)
strings.text: length prefix, then that many bytes, one byte per character, no terminator
strings.characters: the server writes the low byte of each UTF-16 code unit, so values are ASCII in practice; the reference SDK decodes as ASCII. Decode as Latin-1 to never fail

framing.messageLength: header.message_length = total bytes of this message; a datagram can carry several messages back to back
framing.variable: the message's 'variable' array, in array order; it is already in wire order
framing.datagram: a UDP payload is either one or more whole messages back to back, or one jumbo fragment
framing.jumbo: a payload starting with u32 0xFF000000 is a JumboFragmentHeader plus up to 1384 bytes of a larger frame; join fragments with the same (appID, pid, id) in index order 0..count-1, then parse the joined bytes as messages back to back. Senders fragment anything over 1400 bytes

fields.description: always 0xFF000000; a message header can never start with this value

fields.name: id
fields.description: frame id, shared by all fragments of one frame

fields.name: count
fields.description: number of fragments in the frame

messages.description:
CalcSource=Tick records are computed and published each time an option NBBO price changes.  CalcSource=Loop records are computed in a 2-3 minute background loop.
Note that the underlier price (uPrc) will be the same for all options an underlier when CalcSource=Loop.  This is not true for CalcSource=Tick where uPrc will be the underlier price that prevailed when the option price changed.
If you are consuming multicast data and only want records with consistent uPrc values for all options you should ignore Tick records. Alternatively, you can use an independent underlier price source (our StockBookQuote feed or some other) and 'adjust' the values in this table to the new underlier value.
If you are selecting records from SRSE you should note that OptionImpliedQuoteAdj table is a proxy implementation of this table that automatically applies the appropriate underlier adjustments as records are being returned.

messages.description:
EXCHANGE-ASSIGNED IDENTIFIERS - one row per (instrument, venue). The ephemeral, hot half of what
was one ProductMapping table.
| THIS RECORD (exchange)          | ProductMapping (registry/vendor)
lifecycle    | EPHEMERAL - intraday to weekly  | PERMANENT identity
residency    | HOT, resident in every routing  | reference data
| and ingest process              |
writers      | PER-EXCHANGE FEED HANDLERS      | vendor loaders (EDI, GLEIF, OpenFIGI)
volume       | 10^4 - 10^5, churning daily     | one ISIN per instrument
The writer axis is the one that forces it rather than merely favours it - the same reason
SpreadExchID exists as rows instead of a repeater. A table written by per-venue handlers and by
vendor loaders together has two purge horizons and two hot/cold profiles in one resident set.
THERE IS NO extKeyType HERE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. For an exchange-assigned identifier the TYPE
AND THE AUTHORITY ARE THE SAME FACT - 'CBOE's id for this thing' - so the venue IS the type. mic is
key material and no separate type field is needed. That collapses the old venue-scoped-versus-global
question rather than answering it.
